text.headline: Timeline of Colombia
text.text: Major events in the history of Colombia.

events.headline: Earliest Human Settlements
events.text: The earliest evidence of human presence in Colombia dates back to around 10,000 BC, with hunter-gatherer societies inhabiting the region.

events.headline: Spanish Arrival
events.text: Spanish explorers, led by Rodrigo de Bastidas, arrived on the northern coast of Colombia, marking the beginning of European colonization.

events.headline: Foundation of Bogotá
events.text: The city of Bogotá was founded by Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada, becoming a key administrative center for the Spanish Empire in the region.

events.headline: Establishment of the Viceroyalty of New Granada
events.text: The Viceroyalty of New Granada was established, which included present-day Colombia, Ecuador, Panama, and Venezuela, consolidating Spanish power in the region.

events.headline: Independence Movement Begins
events.text: The independence movement in Colombia began with the events of July 20, 1810, leading to a series of conflicts against Spanish rule.

events.headline: Battle of Boyacá
events.text: The Battle of Boyacá was a decisive victory for the patriots during the Colombian War of Independence, leading to the liberation of New Granada.

events.headline: Creation of Gran Colombia
events.text: Gran Colombia was established as a republic, uniting present-day Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, and Panama under a single government.

events.headline: Dissolution of Gran Colombia
events.text: Gran Colombia dissolved into separate nations, leading to the establishment of the Republic of Colombia as an independent state.

events.headline: Panama's Separation
events.text: Panama separated from Colombia with the support of the United States, leading to significant political and economic consequences for Colombia.

events.headline: La Violencia Begins
events.text: La Violencia, a period of intense political violence between liberals and conservatives, began following the assassination of Jorge Eliécer Gaitán.

events.headline: Formation of FARC
events.text: The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) was founded, marking the beginning of a long-standing armed conflict in Colombia.

events.headline: New Constitution
events.text: A new constitution was adopted in Colombia, establishing a more democratic framework and recognizing various rights for citizens.

events.headline: Uribe's Presidency Begins
events.text: Álvaro Uribe was elected president, implementing a security policy aimed at combating guerrilla groups and drug trafficking.

events.headline: Peace Agreement with FARC
events.text: A historic peace agreement was signed between the Colombian government and FARC, officially ending over 50 years of armed conflict.

events.headline: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.text: Colombia, like the rest of the world, faced the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to significant health, economic, and social challenges.

events.headline: Gustavo Petro's Presidency
events.text: Gustavo Petro was elected president, becoming the first leftist leader in Colombia's history, promising significant social and economic reforms.
